claims.text: Severe photophobia or affected vision: prednisolone acetate 1% QID, usually prescribed by an ophthalmologist. Rule out HSV keratitis first (steroids can worsen it)
claims.quote: patients who have severe photophobia or whose vision is affected may benefit from topical corticosteroids (eg, prednisolone acetate 1% drops 4 times a day). Corticosteroids, if prescribed, are usually prescribed by an ophthalmologist. Herpes simplex keratitis must be ruled out first (by fluorescein staining and slit-lamp examination) because corticosteroids can exacerbate it.

claims.text: Topical cyclosporine is less effective but helps when steroid drops are limited by adverse effects
claims.quote: Topical cyclosporin A drops are overall less effective but are helpful if corticosteroid drop use is limited by adverse effects.
